# Conformance checklist: AEF Workflow Designer 0.26.0

GENERATED by tools/build-authoring-kit.py from validate-workflow.py and the dialect
axis. Do not edit; regenerate. Every rule the BPMN form of the validator can emit is
listed. If a finding names a rule that is not here, this file is stale.

## Vocabularies

- Lane `authority`: `authority`, `external`, `initiative`, `none`, `sovereignty`
- Authority -> owner: `authority` -> agent, `initiative` -> agent, `sovereignty` -> human; `none`: no owner can be derived (declared unknown); `external`: performed outside this system, no task compiled (mapping-v1 §3)
- Map `kind` (workflowMeta): `documentation`, `work-plan`; absent = an ordinary process
- Flow-node elements accepted: `boundaryEvent`, `endEvent`, `exclusiveGateway`, `intermediateCatchEvent`, `intermediateThrowEvent`, `parallelGateway`, `scriptTask`, `serviceTask`, `startEvent`, `subProcess`, `task`, `userTask`

## Conventions beyond BPMN 2.0.2

- **Cross-map hand-overs are link events.** A hand-over to another map is drawn as an
  `intermediateThrowEvent` / `intermediateCatchEvent` pair carrying `aef:link`
  (`targetWorkflow`, `name`). BPMN 2.0.2 link events connect sections of ONE process, and
  each map is its own process, so this is an AEF navigation convention. A standards-only
  tool sees both events but cannot infer the cross-process connection. The
  BPMN-standard form, where the two maps are distinct participants, is a message flow in a
  collaboration (optionally a message end event to a message start event).
- **A link catch is an entry, a link throw a terminus.** The validator seeds reachability at
  a catch and draws no dead-end at it (0.15.3); BPMN gives these events no such role.

## Rules

Class: UNIVERSAL = any conformant document satisfies it. DIALECT-RELATIVE = an optional
field the standard does not require is missing: add it, or ignore it as your dialect.
CONVENTIONAL = the standard is silent on this graph shape and our house style expects
it: restructure, or ignore it if the shape is deliberate. PRESENTATIONAL = layout only.
UNCLASSIFIED = the axis has not ruled on it yet (stated, not guessed). The basis column
names what the class rests on: the standard text, a well-formedness ground, the carrier
read, or none.
